steps: Motion is of three types: translatory motion, rotatory motion and vibratory motion.
In translatory motion, a body moves from one place to another. Its particles move the same distance in the same direction in a given time.

Translatory motion may be linear, circular or random. A car moving along a straight road shows linear motion; a stone tied to a string and whirled shows circular motion; and the motion of gas molecules shows random motion.
In rotatory motion, a body spins about an axis passing through it. The spinning of a fan is an example.
In vibratory motion, a body moves to and fro about its mean position. The motion of a simple pendulum is an example.
items.finalAnswer: The three types of motion are translatory, rotatory and vibratory motion; examples include a moving car, a spinning fan and a simple pendulum, respectively.

steps: Draw a distance-time graph with distance on the vertical axis and time on the horizontal axis.
Draw a rising straight line and mark two points on it. Show the change in distance, Δd, and the corresponding change in time, Δt.
The gradient of a distance-time graph is change in distance divided by change in time: gradient = Δd/Δt. It represents speed.
Draw a speed-time graph with speed on the vertical axis and time on the horizontal axis.
Draw a rising straight line and mark two points on it. Show the change in speed, Δv, and the corresponding change in time, Δt.
The gradient of a speed-time graph is change in speed divided by change in time: gradient = Δv/Δt. It represents acceleration.
items.finalAnswer: The gradient of a distance-time graph represents speed; the gradient of a speed-time graph represents acceleration.
